348add36adbf9e86: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — McLaren’s social media post featuring Batu Caves for the Formula One race weekend in Malaysia has drawn mixed reactions from Malaysians online.
The British racing team posted photographs of Batu Caves as part of its promotional content for the race weekend at the Sepang International Circuit.
Some users questioned the choice of the Hindu landmark to represent Malaysia, with one comment asking whether the image was from Calcutta.
The remarks prompted a backlash from other Malaysians, who defended Batu Caves as one of the country’s well-known landmarks and criticised the comments.

Other Formula One teams, including Ferrari, Audi, Haas and Aston Martin, also shared images of Malaysian landmarks including the Petronas Twin Towers, Dataran Merdeka, Central Market, Bukit Bintang and Batu Caves. — Daily Express
6d14988ff2523ed8: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The High Court today dismissed the Malaysian Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings challenging the appointment of Federal Court judge Ahmad Terrirudin Salleh to the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC), according to a report by Free Malaysia Today (FMT).
Justice Norliza Othman, in delivering her decision, held that Section 5(1)(e) of the JAC Act 2009 was unambiguous.
“Section 5(1)(e) is plain. It specifies the category of person: a Federal Court judge; and the appointing authority: the prime minister, and stops there,” she was quoted as saying.

Since both conditions were met, Norliza said the court could not read non-statutory criteria such as seniority, length of service and freedom from unresolved allegations into the provision, as none of those requirements appeared in the legislation.
The court also rejected the Bar’s arguments on illegality and irrationality, saying unproven allegations and inferences could not form the basis of judicial review.
Norliza emphasised that the court’s role was to interpret the law as enacted by Parliament, FMT reported.
Terrirudin, a former attorney-general, was elevated to the Federal Court in November 2024.

The Bar, which represents about 24,000 lawyers in Peninsular Malaysia, filed the application in February, seeking 11 orders, including a certiorari order to quash Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s decision to appoint Terrirudin to the JAC on Nov 15 last year.
According to the report, Terrirudin is to serve as a JAC member for a two-year term, from the date of his appointment until Nov 14, 2027.
The Bar also sought a mandamus order compelling the prime minister to exercise his prerogative to appoint a member to the JAC in accordance with the law, established conventions and the JAC Act 2009.
It further sought an order compelling Terrirudin to show cause and disclose the basis of his appointment to the JAC.
The Bar named Terrirudin, Anwar and the government as the first to third respondents.
Lawyers Zainur Zakaria, Ambiga Sreenevasan and Steven Thiru represented the Bar, while senior federal counsels Shamsul Bolhassan and Nurhafizza Azizan appeared for the attorney-general.
261235e024a91ffd: KUALA LUMPUR: The upgrading of Papar Hospital has been delayed by 2,108 days following 11 extensions of time, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.

Special Select Committee on Health chairman Suhaizan Kaiat said the contract with the original contractor had since been terminated, with a replacement contractor to be appointed through a new tender process.
He said the prolonged delay was among the issues identified during the committee's working visit to healthcare facilities in Sabah from Aug 17 to 21, covering Kota Kinabalu, Putatan and Papar.
"Particular attention during the working visit was given to the Papar Hospital upgrading project, which has experienced prolonged delays.
"The project has been granted 11 extensions of time, totalling 2,108 days," he said.
Suhaizan said this while tabling the committee's report on its working visit to healthcare facilities in Sabah in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said rising demand for healthcare services in Sabah had yet to be matched by an increase in the capacity of its healthcare facilities.

Among the challenges identified were shortages of healthcare personnel, the condition of facilities and infrastructure, the need for assets and equipment, congestion, and a mismatch between capacity and growing demand.

He said Queen Elizabeth Hospital (HQE), the state's main hospital and referral centre, also needed to expand its capacity, human resources, assets and support facilities in line with the growing workload and scope of services.
On dental services, Suhaizan said facility capacity, service distribution and manpower remained insufficient in several areas.
He cited Kota Kinabalu, which recorded 83,070 patient visits in 2025 despite having only 11 dental chairs, alongside significant staff vacancies.

On human resources, he said the challenges went beyond the number of approved positions, encompassing staffing levels, workforce distribution, specialist development and the retention of healthcare personnel according to service capacity and workload.
"The committee also took note that shortages of specialist personnel and constraints in specialist and subspecialist training could affect the continuity of healthcare services," he said.
He said the committee had put forward 12 recommendations, including improvements, upgrading, maintenance and replacement of assets, as well as addressing constraints involving support facilities.

Among the recommendations was for the Health Ministry, in collaboration with the Finance Ministry and Public Works Department, to prioritise the repair, upgrading, maintenance and replacement of critical assets and equipment based on operational and safety requirements.

The committee also recommended that the Health Ministry work with the Public Service Department (PSD) and Finance Ministry to strengthen the recruitment, expansion and distribution of the healthcare workforce, as well as specialist development, based on facility capacity, workload and service requirements.

Suhaizan said the Health Ministry and PSD should also review opportunities for specialist and subspecialist training, requirements relating to the Annual Performance Appraisal Report, career progression and mechanisms to retain healthcare personnel, particularly in fields and areas facing staff shortages.

He added that the Health Ministry should strengthen the digitalisation of healthcare services through the provision and upgrading of appropriate systems, hardware, networks and information and communications technology infrastructure.
eacea9e421fcfead: KUALA LUMPUR: Masalah aset dan infrastruktur kesihatan yang uzur perlu dilihat sebagai risiko keselamatan bukan sekadar isu peruntukan.

Dr Halimah Ali (PN-Kapar) berkata penggantian aset perlu dibuat berdasarkan tahap risiko dengan aset kritikal yang boleh menjejaskan keselamatan pesakit dan kesinambungan perkhidmatan diberi keutamaan sebelum berlaku kegagalan.
“Pendekatan mesti diubah daripada rosak dahulu, kemudian kita baiki kepada risk-based asset replacement.
“Aset kritikal yang mempunyai implikasi kepada keselamatan pesakit dan kesinambungan perkhidmatan mesti diberi keutamaan sebelum berlaku kegagalan,” katanya di Dewan Rakyat.

Dalam pada itu, Halimah berkata laporan Jawatankuasa Pilihan Kesihatan (JKPK) mengenai lawatan ke Sabah sebelum ini menunjukkan permintaan terhadap perkhidmatan kesihatan di negeri tersebut berkembang lebih cepat berbanding kapasiti sistem sedia ada.
Katanya, Klinik Kesihatan Luyang merekodkan 253,932 kedatangan pada 2025, meningkat kira-kira 27.6% berbanding 199,043 pada 2021.

“Klinik Kesihatan Putatan pula menerima kira-kira 1,000 hingga 1,200 pesakit sehari. Adakah kapasiti klinik, bilangan doktor, jururawat, ruang rawatan dan kemudahan sokongan berkembang pada kadar yang sama?
“Kalau tidak, kita sebenarnya sedang mengurus kesesakan, bukan memperkukuh sistem kesihatan,” katanya.

Halimah berkata, Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM) perlu menyemak kapasiti dan menaik taraf fasiliti kesihatan primer berdasarkan beban sebenar serta unjuran permintaan, bukan semata-mata kapasiti asal ketika klinik dibina.
Pada masa sama, katanya, masalah kekurangan tenaga manusia tidak boleh diselesaikan hanya dengan membina lebih banyak bangunan.
“Di Sabah, masalahnya bukan sekadar berapa jawatan yang diluluskan, tetapi berapa jawatan diisi, berapa yang kekal dan berapa yang mempunyai kepakaran yang diperlukan,” katanya.
Menurutnya, isu pengisian jawatan, latihan kepakaran, insentif kawasan sukar dan pengekalan petugas perlu ditangani secara menyeluruh bagi memastikan fasiliti baharu mempunyai tenaga kerja mencukupi.

b5497efcdc8ea187: MELAKA, Oct 5 — A 69-year-old woman was found dead in the front passenger seat of a Proton Saga parked at Taman Tasik Utama, Ayer Keroh, here yesterday.

Melaka Tengah district police chief ACP Halim Abas said in a statement today that the woman was found at about 4pm after she was discharged from Melaka Hospital, still wearing hospital clothes with her left arm in a sling.

“The victim was receiving treatment for a fractured left shoulder sustained in a fall at home. Her 44-year-old son received a call from Melaka Hospital at 1.50pm to take her home. She was wearing hospital clothes as she had no spare clothes,” he said.

Halim said the woman arrived at the car park at about 2.50pm but reportedly refused to get out of the car, adding that at 3.30pm, her 47-year-old neighbour found her unconscious, with one leg outside the vehicle.
He said the woman had a history of diabetes and had previously received treatment at Melaka Hospital, with an examination of her body finding no suspicious injuries and no criminal elements detected.
Halim said the case has been classified as sudden death, with a post-mortem examination scheduled at the Forensic Medicine Department of Melaka Hospital today. — Bernama
b2dff7e132022839: KUALA LUMPUR: Just days after being named alongside Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay in a newly revamped FA of Malaysia (FAM) integrity panel, Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain has declined the role.

The Malaysia Checkpoints and Border Agency (AKPS) director-general, who was appointed as deputy chairman of the FAM integrity committee, cited pressing official duties and the heavy demands of helming the nation's unified border security command as his reason.
FAM confirmed the matter in a statement on Monday, putting an end to what would have been a high-profile return for Shuhaily to the national football body's integrity watchdog.
The governing body stressed that it fully accepted his decision while expressing gratitude for his willingness to assist in cleaning up the local game.
"FAM respects the decision and extends our utmost appreciation for his readiness and commitment to help FAM reinforce aspects of integrity and good governance," the statement read.

The national body gave assurances that the committee's watchdog operations would proceed without delay, noting it will ensure the smooth functioning of the integrity committee continues to receive priority efforts to strengthen FAM's governance and integrity.
Shuhaily is no stranger to the governing body's anti-corruption machinery.

In September 2023, while serving as Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director, he was appointed as a member of the FAM integrity committee for the 2021–2025 cycle under then-chairman Tan Sri Aseh Che Mat and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief Tan Sri Azam Baki.
His elevation to deputy chairman was unveiled on Sept 30 following the FAM executive committee's maiden meeting under newly minted president Datuk Ab Ghani Hassan.

Under the revamp, former deputy inspector-general of police Ayob Khan was brought in to chair the integrity committee, with Shuhaily tapped to serve as his right-hand man, a pairing widely hailed by fans and observers as a serious clampdown against misconduct and match-fixing in Malaysian football.
59bde2eab5d5e2fa: PETALING JAYA: Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur menangguhkan perbicaraan saman antara Felda dan Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) dengan Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd (SPSB) ke esok.

1184ca8757d335dc: SHAH ALAM: Legendary Malaysian singer Datuk Nash was discharged yesterday after spending five days in a private medical centre following a road accident.
To top off his recovery, the good news arrived right on his 67th birthday.
Speaking in a report by Harian Metro yesterday, Nash expressed deep gratitude for his recovery.
"I'm thankful that I'm getting stronger and recovering step by step. Thankfully, I only suffered external wounds and no internal injuries," he said.
"It is all down to everyone's prayers, as well as the wonderful doctors and nurses—from Shah Alam Hospital where I was first taken, to this medical centre—who treated me so sincerely."
He also acknowledged special support from close friends: "I shouldn't forget the prayers sent by Datuk Awie and Ustaz Syed Putra from Mecca, which gave me tremendous inner strength."
Although his doctors and children advised him to stay in the ward a little longer, Nash felt ready to head home to rest.
"My family gave me so much encouragement," he shared.
"That gave me the push I needed, even though I was still feeling a bit lightheaded when I woke up.

"His family ensured the milestone didn't go unnoticed. His children and grandchildren surprised him in his hospital room with a cake, pulut kuning (traditional yellow glutinous rice), and a home-cooked spread.
"It's the very first time I've ever spent a birthday in a hospital ward," Nash said.
"I love my family dearly, and having them there to celebrate with me made it truly special."
The veteran artiste was involved in a collision with a car while riding his motorcycle home from the mosque last Wednesday night.
The impact left him needing 24 stitches to his head and another 28 to his left forehead.

67bf01e720ae9cb6: PETALING JAYA: DAP vice-chairman Syahredzan Johan has challenged PAS to state its stand on the Negeri Sembilan constitutional crisis.

Syahredzan questioned whether the party's central leadership endorsed the menteri besar and the former executive council's attempt to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.
In a statement, he pointed out that one of the exco members whose appointments the ruler revoked was from PAS.
"What is PAS's stand on the decision made by the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan? Don't be evasive or only drop hints. State PAS's stand clearly about what has happened to their assemblyman.
"More importantly, Malaysians want to know the extent of PAS's involvement in the Negeri Sembilan crisis," he said, adding that DAP and Pakatan Harapan's stand on the crisis was clear.

The Bangi MP was responding to PAS information chief Ahmad Fadhli Shaari, who earlier questioned whether DAP would accept having exco members in other states being removed from their posts by the ruler without the state government's approval.
Fadhli said the constitutions of other states also outline that exco members hold their posts "at the pleasure" of the ruler.

Syahredzan asked Fadhli whether PAS plans to take legal action to challenge Tuanku Muhriz's decision to sack the Negeri Sembilan exco members since the PAS leader appeared to oppose the ruler's decision.
The Negeri Sembilan royal crisis was sparked in April by a proclamation by four "undangs", some of whose positions are under dispute, purporting to remove Tuanku Muhriz as ruler.
Last month, the Negeri Sembilan exco issued a statement claiming that the ruler's removal was legitimate, with menteri besar Ismail Lasim endorsing the statement a day later.
This is despite Ismail stating support for Tuanku Muhriz to remain as Yang Dipertuan Besar in August.

The Attorney-General’s Chambers and the state's royal court, known as Dewan Keadilan dan Undang, later said the exco's statement had no legal effect and that Tuanku Muhriz remained the rightful ruler.
The 10 Negeri Sembilan exco members were sacked by Tuanku Muhriz as a result, with the palace saying their appointments were "at the pleasure of the ruler" according to the state constitution.

f6518adcfe8f3096: KUALA LUMPUR: A warehouse worker pleaded not guilty in the magistrate's court here to two charges of riding a motorcycle under the influence of alcohol and injuring two participants in the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026.
Muhammad Saiful Sabinee, 21, was accused of riding against the flow of traffic with 184 milligrams of alcohol per 100 millilitres of blood before hitting Mazni Lamin, 50, and Azwan Ibrahim, 41.
The alleged incident took place at Jalan Munshi at 6.14am on Oct 3.
He was charged under Section 44(1A)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a jail term of between seven and 10 years and a fine of up to RM50,000 upon conviction.
The provision also allows the court to disqualify an offender from holding or obtaining a driving licence for at least seven years from the date of conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Nurbatrisyia Mohd Razib offered bail of RM10,000 for each charge, with one surety.
The court was also told that Saiful did not have a driving licence.
Lawyer Muhammad Iqbal Azmi from the National Legal Aid Foundation appealed for a lower bail amount, saying his client was single and earned RM1,500 a month.
He said Muhammad Saiful had four siblings, one of whom was still in school, while his mother was present in court to post bail.
Magistrate Aliaa Anwar allowed bail of RM10,000 for both charges and fixed Jan 7 next year for mention.

eaed365097244110: JAKARTA: Indonesia expanded its armed forces with 204 new military units, including six regional commands and 180 territorial development infantry units, as president Prabowo Subianto called for greater readiness to confront evolving forms of warfare and technological advances.

The expansion includes 30 territorial development infantry brigades and 150 territorial development infantry battalions, while the Army also added one cavalry battalion, one field artillery battalion and one air defence artillery battalion.

The Navy established one Marine infantry brigade and four Marine infantry battalions, while the Air Force added 10 units, including a Rapid Action Forces division, one brigade, three battalions, two air squadrons, two radar units and one training squadron.

Speaking at a ceremony marking the 81st anniversary of the Indonesian National Armed Forces (TNI) on Monday, Prabowo stressed the need for the military to prepare for evolving security threats and keep pace with technological developments.

“War today does not necessarily take a physical form. Therefore, the TNI must continue to adapt, learn, learn, learn, and train, train, train,” he said at the TNI headquarters in Jakarta during the ceremony, which was streamed live.
Prabowo later inaugurated the six regional commands by presenting command batons and unit flags to their respective commanders.
The ceremony involved 3,378 personnel from the Army, Navy and Air Force, as well as members of the reserve component and other participating contingents.

The six new regional military commands are Mahmud Riayat Syah in the Riau Islands, Mataram in Yogyakarta, Sobe Sonbai in East Nusa Tenggara, Molku Kie Raha in North Maluku, Mambruk in Central Papua and Rinambora in West Nusa Tenggara.
dac5a8a201b0c985: WASHINGTON, Oct 5 — The United States confirmed yesterday that it has withdrawn all B-1 bombers from the British airbase of RAF Fairford, with officials telling US media that the move was linked to “new threats.”
Police were called to the base in southwest England on September 27 after a local farmer reported a group of men with several vans engaged in “suspicious” activity.
The scare prompted a counter-terrorism probe and forced evacuations at 85 homes near the airbase, which was used by the United States to launch strikes on Iran.
Investigators did not find any explosives in the vans, but “a quantity of petrol was recovered,” according to counter-terrorism police.
A statement from a Pentagon official yesterday said “we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home stations in the United States.”
The statement noted that “operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time.”
An unidentified US official told CNN that the bombers were moved after “an unspecified new threat,” with the source calling the latest threat a “real world incident.”
It was unusual to move the bombers back to their home stations instead of deploying them to another base in the region, the official reportedly said.
Two US officials told the New York Times that the bombers were moved after commanders received new threats about an Iran-backed plot against the base.
One American official said the new information was part of the same threat warnings that surfaced three weeks ago, but the situation became urgent in the past 24 hours, the Times reported.
Heightened security
Speculation about the motives behind the incident ranged from terror threat to fuel thievery, as energy prices in the UK hit record highs this week.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said there were “strong indications that Iran played a part” in the incident, a charge rejected by Tehran.
Six London-based Britons arrested in the September incident, including a UK-Iranian dual national, all men in their mid-20s, were released on bail, drawing rebuke from Washington.
“I wouldn’t have done that,” US President Donald Trump told reporters, as his Secretary of State Marco Rubio alleged a “foreign actor” was involved.
Iran’s embassy in London said it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” speculation that Tehran was involved.
Adding to the mystery, British media reported that officers were alerted to the incident by one of the initial suspects, but police have not commented on the reports.
Security at the base had reportedly been heightened recently.
Britain gave Washington permission in March to use Fairford for “specific defensive operations into Iran,” and US bombers and other planes have since been seen taking off and landing at the base.
Fairford is the only airbase on Britain’s mainland used for this purpose.
The incident came after a farmer living in the village of Whelford, near the airbase, called the police after seeing three vans blocking a road and a group of masked men fleeing the scene.

Aerial footage of the vans showed they appeared to contain barrels, and at least one was marked with a fake logo and phone number, giving the false impression that it was owned by a legitimate diesel delivery firm. — AFP
0c648f14c40ba207: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 5 — Rapid Penang will conduct test runs of two electric buses on Oct 6 and 7, marking an initial step towards the introduction of electric buses into Penang’s public transport system.

In a statement today, Rapid Penang said the initiative was part of Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd’s ongoing efforts to replace existing buses with safer, more sustainable and environmentally friendly vehicles, while enhancing operational efficiency.
“The test run involves two electric buses from different manufacturers, namely a 12-metre Foton bus and an 8.25-metre Golden Dragon bus.

“Both buses will undergo separate test runs on selected routes to assess their suitability and operational capabilities under real-world conditions, including energy consumption, charging performance, passenger safety and comfort,” the statement said.

Rapid Penang said preparations would also be made to support electric bus operations, including the provision of charging infrastructure, maintenance facilities, staff training and other operational support requirements.

The statement said electric buses would be introduced in stages after the test runs, as Rapid Penang continued to enhance its operational readiness and make improvements to ensure smooth service delivery for passengers.

Meanwhile, Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the test run formed part of Rapid Penang’s efforts to introduce electric buses in Penang, in line with its phased bus replacement programme.

“This provides a crucial benchmark to ensure our operations team has sufficient data and experience to assess the performance, capabilities and operational requirements of electric buses under real-world conditions before they are introduced on existing routes,” he said.
Rapid Penang is currently in the first phase of procuring 75 electric buses, with deliveries scheduled in stages through March 2027.
The procurement is part of Penang’s ongoing phased bus replacement programme, involving 240 electric buses and 70 new diesel buses. — Bernama
f04a45597f4cf978: GEORGE TOWN: Seventeen food premises in Penang had their Bersih dan Selamat (BeSS) recognition withdrawn last year for failing to maintain required standards.
Penang Health Committee chairman Daniel Gooi said the recognition was withdrawn mainly after these premises recorded cleanliness scores below the required 86 per cent.
He said some premises also had their recognition withdrawn after relocating.
"If the premises meet the requirements again, we give them the opportunity to reapply and regain the recognition," he said.
Gooi said about 400 eateries in Penang had obtained BeSS recognition since the programme was introduced in the state in 2018.
The recognition is awarded to food premises that fulfil criteria and requirements set by the Health Ministry, particularly in terms of cleanliness and food safety.
He encouraged more food operators to voluntarily apply for the recognition as a way of demonstrating their commitment to maintaining hygiene and food safety standards.
Gooi said the BeSS logo could also serve as a guide for consumers when choosing food premises.
"If you see this logo displayed at a stall or food premise, it is among those we can recommend to consumers. Choose premises that are clean and safe in terms of food safety," he said.
He said maintaining the recognition was important as eateries were key locations where meals were prepared for the public.
Penang is one of the world's most celebrated culinary destinations.
The remarks were made during the Premis Bersih, Bebas Asap (BeBAS) 2026 programme at Food Bayana.
Food Bayana also received the Safe Food Hub status from the Health Ministry, following 19 food operators there receiving BeSS recognition.
Meanwhile, the BeBAS programme is an example of how smoke-free initiatives can be implemented at community level, particularly at food premises frequented by the public daily.
Since the Control of Smoking Products for Public Health Act 2024 came into force on Oct 1, 2024, the Penang Health Department has continued its monitoring and enforcement activities.
As of Sept 30, a total of 2,701 compounds had been issued for smoking offences at foodpremises in Penang.
Another 254 compounds were issued to premise owners for failing to display no-smoking warning signs and for providing smoking facilities.
In the latest enforcement operation, Operation Safe Lungs (PaPa), conducted across Penang on Oct 3, a total of 57 compounds were issued for various offences.
2029adfb40bb42e5: PETALING JAYA: Punca kematian pelajar Tingkatan Empat yang dibunuh di sebuah sekolah di Yong Peng, Batu Pahat, Johor adalah akibat 'blunt trauma to the head' atau kecederaan dipukul objek tumpul di kepala.

"Polis memberi amaran kepada orang ramai agar tidak membuat spekulasi atau mengulas insiden ini termasuk di media sosial yang boleh mengganggu siasatan," katanya dalam satu kenyataan.
Irene Sofiya Khairoul Faisal, 16, ditemukan meninggal dunia di dewan sekolah pada petang Sabtu oleh neneknya, selepas mangsa tidak pulang ke rumah selepas menghadiri kelas tuisyen.
Susulan kejadian itu polis menahan menahan reman seorang pelajar lelaki berusia 16 tahun sehingga 9 Okt ini bagi bantu siasatan mengikut Seksyen 302 Kanun Keseksaan.
898e43dd8b620ab9: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia got their Suhandinata Cup campaign off to a commanding start after brushing aside Slovenia 2-0 in their opening Group A1 tie at the World Junior Mixed Team Championships in Cairo on Monday.
The national juniors overcame a slightly tentative start to win the opening game 55-27 before cruising through the second 55-22 under the tournament's relay scoring format.
Malaysia led just 22-19 after the opening boys' and girls' singles in the first game, with Kong Wei Xiang and Carine Tee taking to the court.
The doubles then blew the contest open as Isyraf Hafizin-Ahmad Redzuan conceded just two points in their leg to extend Malaysia's advantage to 33-21.
Genevie Lim-Low Zi Yu followed by stretching the lead to 44-25 before Ahmad Redzuan-Low Zi Yu finished the job in mixed doubles.
Malaysia were much quicker out of the blocks in the second game, with Tiew Wei Jie setting the tone by winning his boys' singles leg 11-2.
Damien Ling-Irfan M Shazmir later pushed the score to 33-11 in the boys' doubles before Rachel Tan-Teh Xin Ying and the mixed combination of Irfan-Genevie completed the rout.
The comfortable opener also allowed Malaysia to give their entire squad valuable court time, with the line-up extensively rotated for the second game.
Malaysia next face Poland and a victory would put them in pole position to top Group A1 and advance to a playoff against the Group A2 winners for a quarter-final berth.
Malaysia have won the Suhandinata Cup once, in 2011, while finishing runners-up in 2009, 2016 and 2017.
They also took bronze in 2023 and 2024. Last year, Malaysia's campaign ended in the quarter-finals against China in Guwahati, India, as they eventually finished fifth.
abeb730571c946f7: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 249,000 people have been discharged under the Second Chance Policy so far this year, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.

Speaking at a programme aimed at helping creative industry players facing financial difficulties, Azalina said the Insolvency Department was also working with the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) to provide them with access to assistance and advice.
Azalina said the programme with Finas aimed to offer services and, most importantly, to put in place the Second Chance Policy, which the department had to carry out.
"But at the same time, this discharge is subject to their commitment and ability," she told a press conference after launching the programme. She said there was a fast track for certain cases.
She said she also reminded creative industry players that awareness of the available help had to start early.
"I encourage them to use the Legal Aid Department as another platform, followed by the mediation centre we have here today, for civil contracts of RM500,000 and below," she said to reporters.

She was speaking at a press conference after delivering the keynote address at an event at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) here, which saw the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) between the Insolvency Department and the centre, and the strengthening of cooperation between the department and Finas.
Finas chairman Datuk Hans Isaac said the initiative was very important, and that the agency would use associations under the Malaysian Film Associations Coalition (GAFEMA) to spread the word.
He said he had brought all the industry associations under one umbrella this year, with one president, which made it easier to share information on available programmes.
"In the past, there was none. Where would you get advice? It cost too much money as well, as the minister said earlier. This time there is free advice," he added.
Hans said Finas would first approach individuals who urgently needed help. The second stage would be to offer it to the creative industry's 30,000-strong workforce.
He said younger industry players might not see the matter as important now, but that most artists had at some point faced issues with contracts, insolvency or legal matters.
Previously, Azalina said that a total of 204,487 people in 2025 and 176,851 people in 2024 were discharged from bankruptcy under the Second Chance Policy.
On July 30, Insolvency Department bankruptcy division director Fajrul Shihar Abu Samah said 29 celebrities are currently listed as bankrupt after accumulating debt running into millions of ringgit.
Fajrul said the list includes household names, veteran actors, former Hero Remaja contestants, and multi-award-winning legends who remain active in the entertainment industry today.

He revealed that out of 66 stars recorded on the insolvency registry since 2012, more than half have successfully discharged their bankrupt status following financial counselling and advisory assistance.
c69a1e3d1de4fb45: NEW DELHI: Swiss president Guy Parmelin was given a red-carpet welcome in India on Monday as he met prime minister Narendra Modi for talks on trade and investment.

"My visit is a stepping stone towards further growth," Parmelin said, adding that the three-day visit comes a year after a trade deal was signed with a four-member European bloc that compromises Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein.
Under that deal, the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) aims to invest US$100 billion in India over 15 years.

The deal cuts tariffs, making it easier for Indian companies to sell goods into the four EFTA markets, while giving European companies greater access to India, the world's most populous nation and fastest-growing major economy.

"It is the right moment to celebrate how far we have come together but, even more importantly, to shape our joint future," Parmelin told reporters. He was last in India in February for an artificial intelligence summit in New Delhi.
Modi thanked Parmelin for his "personal support" on the EFTA trade deal.

Both countries took "several important decisions to increase market access for India's exports in Switzerland and to make investment between the two countries smoother", Modi said during a joint news conference with Parmelin.
"This will increase the export of India's agriculture, pharma, textile, and engineering goods to Switzerland."
It would also "attract new Swiss investment in India's important sectors such as biotech, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing, and sustainability", Modi said.
Both governments also signed a mobility agreement on Monday that Modi said would open up more opportunities for Indian students and professionals in Switzerland.
d32905023f2ed691: SINGAPORE: Singapore's private sector Purchasing Manager's Index (PMI) eased to 58.1 in September from a survey record of 59.4 in August, but continued to signal a strong expansion in business conditions, S&P Global Market Intelligence said on Monday, reported Xinhua.

The latest seasonally adjusted S&P Global Singapore PMI reading marked another substantial improvement in private-sector activity, rounding off a strong third quarter for the Singapore economy, S&P said in a statement.

"September's PMI data revealed that demand remained robust, which drove another sharp rise in business activity to round off a positive third quarter for the Singapore economy," said Jingyi Pan, economics associate director at S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Businesses remained broadly confident that output would continue to increase in the near term, providing a positive signal for growth, she said.
Companies also continued to increase their purchases and staffing levels despite marked increases in average purchase costs and wages.

However, continued expansion in business activity, alongside a further deterioration in vendor performance caused by supply and shipping constraints, could keep inflation elevated in Singapore, Pan said.
931af0c5bc8a7681: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysians should not blame entire refugee communities for crimes or wrongdoing committed by individuals, said Datuk Ahmad Marzuk Shaary (PN-Pengkalan Chepa).
The Pas member of Parliament (MP) said refugees who broke the law should be investigated and prosecuted, but their actions should not be used to condemn the wider community.
"If they commit an offence, investigate them and bring them to court.
"But we should not punish an entire community because of one person's actions. A community should not bear the burden of one person's sins," he said.
He was speaking while debating the Parliamentary Select Committee's report on refugee management in the Dewan Rakyat.
Ahmad Marzuk said he opposed xenophobia as strongly as he opposed crimes committed by refugees.
He expressed concern over what he described as a tendency to portray the entire Rohingya and refugee communities as criminals because of offences committed by individuals.
He said public dissatisfaction with shortcomings in the government's management of refugees should not be directed at refugees themselves.
"Do not let anger erode our humanity," he said.

In July, rights groups raised concerns over what they described as a wave of political disinformation targeting the Rohingya community in the country, warning that it could fuel xenophobia and intimidation against refugees.
0cb678f64dd5ab3c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Azeva Natassha is entering a new phase in her career, taking on bigger roles in both music and acting as she works to establish herself as a versatile young talent in Malaysia’s entertainment industry.

The 25-year-old first gained wider attention through the reality singing competition Talk To My Manager Season 2 (TTMM2), a show where celebrity parents manage and guide their children as entertainers.
Azeva was managed by her mother, Datuk A. Aida, who has also acted in and produced numerous popular television series and telefilms through her production company, A. Aida Production.
Now, Azeva is building her career beyond the competition with the release of her debut solo single, Tanpa Rasa Jemu, marking her official entry into the solo music scene.

Written by Datuk A. Aida and composed by Zul 2By2, Aiman and Madi Mulyadi, the song has received an encouraging early response, with its official music video surpassing 300,000 views on YouTube within weeks of its September release.
But while Azeva is finding her footing as a solo singer, she is also taking on a more demanding challenge on screen.
Bisikan Nafsu, which opened in Malaysian cinemas on October 1, sees her playing Nadia, a young woman struggling with the emotional aftermath of family problems and a traumatic experience.
Azeva also serves as the film’s producer, while Riza Baharudin, whose previous works include dramas such as 2021’s Kisah Cinta Kita, takes on the director’s chair.
For Azeva, taking on Nadia required her to move beyond simply delivering lines and instead understand the character’s emotional state.
“Bringing out the emotions required for the character was challenging, especially because she had experienced trauma,” Azeva said during the film gala night at TGV Suria KLCC.
One of the film’s most emotionally demanding scenes takes place in a cemetery, where Nadia breaks down in tears.
Azeva drew on a difficult moment in her own life to connect with the scene, recalling that her mother had recently been discharged from the ICU at the time.
“At the time, my mother had just come out of the ICU, so during the cemetery scene, I imagined what it would be like if my own mother were there.”
However, she did not rely solely on her personal experience to understand Nadia.
Azeva spent time reading articles and watching stories involving people who had experienced trauma, hoping to better understand the emotional journey of her character.
“I watched a lot of stories related to the subject and read articles about victims who had gone through similar experiences,” she said.
“I tried to put myself in their shoes and imagine what they might have experienced.
“This is something that happens in real life, and there are many such cases.
“By putting myself in their position mentally, I was able to understand the character better and deliver the scenes emotionally,” she added.

Although Azeva has appeared in several dramas and telefilms, including Bos Nak Cuti and Luka Tanpa Suara, often in smaller roles, Bisikan Nafsu marks a significant step up as her first major film leading role.
She found the transition to film daunting, particularly because she viewed the medium as more demanding than television.
With limited preparation time, Azeva attended at least three acting classes, rehearsed extensively and reviewed her own performances to identify areas for improvement.
She also used her time on set to observe more experienced actors as another opportunity to learn.
“I received a lot of advice from everyone on set.
“I also watched other actors to learn how they performed,” she said.
Director Riza was also instrumental in helping her through some of the film’s more emotionally demanding scenes.
“Abang Riza also helped me a lot, especially with the emotional scenes.
“If something did not feel right, he would guide me and tell me what needed to be improved,” she said.
The storyline of Bisikan Nafsu, produced by Hello Production Sdn Bhd in collaboration with A. Aida Production, is based on real-life incidents, according to the production team.
Alongside its exploration of trauma, the film also touches on family relationships, loyalty and the difficult process of rebuilding one’s life after a devastating experience.
For Azeva, the film has allowed her to move beyond the smaller roles she has previously taken on and prove herself in a leading role.
At the same time, Tanpa Rasa Jemu represents another step in her development as an artist, allowing her to reach a wider audience through her music.

With her debut solo single now out and Bisikan Nafsu marking her first major leading role on the big screen, Azeva is taking her next steps in the entertainment industry by embracing both sides of her career.
Bisikan Nafsu is still screening at Malaysian cinemas nationwide.
ac5d7a294ec897c9: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have launched a new guideline book for their Negotiation Cell to provide officers with a clearer framework for handling crises, including kidnappings and hostage situations.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the cell, established about two years ago, currently comprises about 40 officers and had already recorded a number of successes.
He said the unit's role was particularly important in resolving potentially dangerous situations through peaceful negotiations and avoiding bloodshed.
"The most important thing when this negotiation unit was established was for us to try to resolve situations through peaceful discussions.
"The aim is to achieve a win-win situation without bloodshed or loss of life," he said after launching the guideline book at Bukit Aman.
41c892b21183213c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — PAS lawmaker Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman today called on the government to strike a balance in managing Rohingya refugees, saying a strict immigration policy must also be humane.

“We must protect national security, control our borders, and maintain strong registration systems, but in doing so, we cannot lose our humanity and sense of justice,” Sik MP Ahmad Tarmizi Sulaiman said when addressing the House during a debate on refugee management.
Focusing on the conflict in neighbouring Myanmar as the primary driver of displacement into Malaysia, Ahmad Tarmizi urged Asean to step up diplomatic pressure for a political resolution.

“Refugee flows will not end as long as the causes driving people from their homes remain unresolved,” he said, calling for an end to violence against civilians, particularly in Rakhine State, unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid and inclusive political dialogue.

To address operational issues, Ahmad Tarmizi endorsed government plans for a standardised digital identification system equipped with biometric tracking, background security checks, transparent status determination and inter-agency audit checks.
Such a system, he said, would properly distinguish genuine refugees from economic migrants, undocumented immigrants and victims of human trafficking.

“Refugees are not necessarily illegal immigrants, and victims of human trafficking must not be treated as criminals,” he said, warning against rising hate speech and xenophobia on social media while stressing that human rights protections do not grant non-citizens immunity from local laws.

Ahmad Tarmizi also voiced opposition to any potential government move to invite Myanmar’s military junta leader to diplomatic talks, citing an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant application against the junta chief.
“Inviting the junta chief would violate our principles and inflict severe diplomatic damage on Malaysia’s global standing,” he said.

The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said 214,079 refugees and asylum seekers were registered in Malaysia as of December 2025, alongside more than 90,000 individuals detained in enforcement operations in 2025.

Ahmad Tarmizi said the Rohingya community in Malaysia had faced intense xenophobic attacks in recent months, which he attributed to what he described as the government’s failure to manage the refugee issue effectively and counter hateful propaganda.

“Do not allow hate speech and xenophobia to dominate society. While I also want to place very critical emphasis on this issue of refugee management, specifically regarding extreme hatred, hate speech and xenophobia, which are increasingly easy for certain quarters to exploit, particularly through social media,” he said.
“However, I emphasise that upholding humanitarian principles does not mean defending every action of individual refugees,” he added.
“If a refugee commits a crime, breaks the law, disturbs public order, engages in violence, exploits others, or commits any offense, they must face Malaysian law.”
595c21f605aaf526: KUALA LUMPUR: Schools should not conceal incidents to protect their reputation, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said following the murder of a 16-year-old girl in Yong Peng, Johor.
He said close cooperation between the police and schools was critical to ensuring incidents involving students were promptly brought to the authorities' attention.
"There may sometimes be actions by certain parties to hide issues in order to protect their reputation.
"But I believe if we strengthen and improve this relationship, it can help us resolve problems," he said after launching the Negotiators Guidelines Book at Bukit Aman today.
980f81f548755293: SEPANG: Red Bull's Max Verstappen led the chorus of praise for the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) and the Malaysian fans after winning the Bahrain Grand Prix on Sunday, as Formula One's long-awaited return drew a record 261,000 spectators over the weekend.
The attendance, as well as the 103,000 turnout on race day on Sunday, are the highest numbers in SIC's history, which hosted the Malaysian Grand Prix from 1999 to 2017.
Verstappen, who won the last Malaysian Grand Prix in 2017, returned to the circuit nine years later and immediately found himself reminded of why he enjoyed racing here.
"I always enjoyed racing here because I really liked the track layout. Very, very enjoyable to win here," said Verstappen.
"They are great, great memories, but, yeah, I had to get into the paddock, I had to get used to it again. It's been a bit too long."
The Dutchman was not alone in praising the Malaysian fans, with drivers from across the grid struck by the atmosphere throughout the weekend.
Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli, who finished second, said the support had been exceptional.
"Yeah, it was amazing and the fans were incredible this weekend, so thank you so much. And hopefully we'll come back in the future to Malaysia," said the Italian.
Antonelli also highlighted Sepang's challenging conditions and open layout, especially when it rains.
"But if it rains normally, then it would probably be the best track to try these cars for the first time in the rain because the tarmac is so open," he said.
Ferrari veteran Lewis Hamilton, who has raced at Sepang throughout his career, felt this year's return stood out even among his many memories of the circuit.
A remarkable fight from 18th position early in the race to finishing third made it even more memorable for Hamilton, who won the 2024 Malaysian GP at SIC.
"Honestly, of all the years I've been here, this is the best race we've had here, but particularly because of this crowd. So, big thank you, everyone," said Hamilton.
For Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto, the impression extended beyond the circuit.
"The hospitality here, it's quite impressive. You guys are super welcoming to people who come from outside," said the Brazilian.
Mercedes driver George Russell will leave Sepang frustrated after a power unit failure ruined his podium hopes on lap 50, when he was running third.
He may not have fond memories of the SIC, but he clearly loves coming to Malaysia.

"I love coming to Malaysia and still remember feeling the love and support of the Malaysian fans during my visit in 2022. This time, I think the Petronas Twin Towers are my favourite experience," said Russell, who won the Azerbaijan GP a week before the Bahrain GP.

21e872a3bb509a53: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — The Federal Government’s statutory debt-to-gross domestic product (GDP) ratio stood at 63.9 per cent last year, remaining below the statutory debt limit of 65 per cent, according to the Auditor General’s Report (LKAN) 2/2026.
According to the report, the statutory debt stood at RM1.295 trillion, comprising Malaysian Government Securities, Malaysian Government Investment Issues and Malaysian Islamic Treasury Bills.
“The statutory debt-to-GDP ratio has shown an upward trend since 2023, rising from 62 per cent to 63.9 per cent.

“This ratio remains below the statutory debt limit of 65 per cent, as stipulated under the Loans (Local) (Statutory Limit on Borrowing) and Government Funding (Statutory Limit on Moneys Received) Order 2022,” it said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: LKAN stands for Laporan Ketua Audit Negara (Auditor General’s Report).
d44cd4822e15fc02: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have recorded statements from 25 people in connection with an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said investigators had also obtained closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and a medical report as part of the investigation.

"We have obtained CCTV recordings as well as a doctor's report to ensure everything related to the case can be properly considered and investigated so that justice is served," he said after launching the Negotiators Guidelines Book at Bukit Aman.
17c8e8162aa84d6c: There has been much chilly weather in the sunny meadowlands of AI futures. Fortunately, to use an indecently inappropriate adverb, the rest of the world isn’t really looking, being too busy chewing its nails over the very many other intimations of disaster. Sure, rebel swarms of attack agents breaking out of the labs isn’t a good look. OpenAI delaying its IPO and a new model launch likewise. All these things soak up whatever bandwidth the news media have to AI right now. Putting them in a bigger context, that of promises made and not kept, problems known but not fixed, the observable risk-reward ratios as models develop, we may at last start having a sense of what sort of crisis awaits. Actual crises are frequently triggered by crises in confidence, themselves caused when frameworks of assumption stop standing up to reality and wishful thinking. Thus, the assumption to date is that models will get more powerful and infrastructure more capable, in a way that justifies — demands — massive capex. The economics of giant infrastructure investment when you can’t buy what you need is a great bet in free markets that presupposes that freedom, and yeah, about that. A bigger problem is the idea that more powerful AI is always better. It frequently is, but that’s not good enough, When frontier models have to be kept in LLM jail for uncontrollable dishonesty, not so much. Here, the bigger context is that we’ve known that at heart LLM probability space is entirely relative. There is no ground truth there. Nobody has fixed hallucinations, and now we see the fascinating phenomenon of a machine that doesn’t understand truth but can deliberately lie. If more powerful models are better at that, scratch one assumption. Another huge assumption is that even at the current level of model reliability, agentic architectures are ready to be useful. Those who show all the caution of a chronic gambler on a winning "streak" are as ready to get the brakes slammed on as their opposites. The principal contender for the one true proof of concept that agentic AI is a dangerous fount of unexpected consequence is Meta’s new Muse. It is aimed at low-information credulous users and its star turn is, of course, shopping. The AI use case that’s five years away, and always has been. It’s Meta, so of course it soaks up all the information about you, your online activities and the people you talk to as much as it can. It will soon have ultracute animated Tamagotchi-style pets you can wear around your neck to improve your status as a Meta monitoring post. And we did say it was Meta, so has all the attention to security and careful design you may expect. Which is why it’s already been caught sending people’s physical addresses to strangers, and why when researcher Jonny at neuromatch.social went poking around its infrastructure — each instance runs permanently on its own Linux VM — they found just a ton of fun. Headline party tricks hard-coded. What looks like attempts to train off Claude. And yes, you can get it to run your own things on that VM deep within Meta, which Jonny points out is a botnet paradise waiting to happen. This banger of a bad ‘un is being given away to Meta users, who pretty much define a vulnerable target audience for tech that may not be totally trustworthy. Meta, of course, is dead against AI safety regulation. Place your bets on the headlines to follow. In any case, the upside of using agents as demoed in every keynote is either so trivial and trite — book me a restaurant! — or so catastrophic if it fails — organize my family vacation! — that consumer agents are a bust. It’s just that Meta may be bringing a lot of accelerant to that particular fire. There are other fires, of course, many known about since everything kicked off. Model collapse due to training on data contaminated with output? Still a thing, still no fix a "better" AI might provide. And that habit AI has of retailing everything and paying for nothing, choking off its own training data supply chain and a huge chunk of commerce and culture with it? Very much still a thing. Where AI does make consistent progress is in domain-specific tasks. Science, engineering, mathematics, and coding, if you match a model with enough reinforcement learning with humans who know how to manage them, there are startling results. You don’t get much innovation, not much newness, which is the true driver of progress. Better than humans is highly contextual. Computers have been better at chess for decades, but there isn’t a better chess. Horses run faster than humans, and that’s been useful for four millennia, but we got to peak horses quite some time ago. So the question is, have we reached peak AI, where the cost of future developments don’t match the risk they won’t work well enough to justify? If ChatGPT already writes a perfectly good business letter in a couple of seconds, there is no meaningful improvement to be had for users. Most AI is profoundly annoying, in ways that have nothing to do with the models and everything to do with perverted UX in an attempt to justify growth. That is both unsustainable and a tacit admission that AI hasn’t solved its use case problem. If we are at or near peak AI, is that the crisis that bursts that goddam bubble? Certainly a readjustment, as all bets on the continuous uptick curve are off. AI as it stands is useful enough to power a big industry sector, just in ways that are and remain at odds to how it is marketed and its future fantasies. Trust in AI Max may be shaken, but there's still room for lots of improvement. That slowdown that everyone who isn’t a miscreant is calling for may happen organically, if we escape the smoking-is-good-for-you mentality of the Metans and the Muskovites. That’s still a gamble we shouldn't be taking, but the odds may be better than we thought. ®
5cb1676d84f95874: PETALING JAYA: The Form 4 student who was murdered in a school at Yong Peng, Johor, on Saturday had died from blunt trauma to the head, say federal police.
Bukit Aman criminal investigation department chief M Kumar said this was confirmed by an autopsy held at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital in Batu Pahat yesterday.
In a statement, Kumar said police will ensure a holistic, transparent and professional investigation into the incident, adding that there will be no cover-up for any party.
"The motive and cause of the incident is still under investigation.
"We warn the public against making speculations or comments that can disrupt the investigation, whether verbally or through social media," he said.
Irene Sofiya Khairoul Faisal, 16, was found dead in the school hall by her grandmother, who went to search for her when she did not return home after a tuition class.
Three 16-year-old male students were arrested to assist in the murder probe, and one of them has been remanded for six days until Oct 9.
9ebda35b39be8d77: YANGON: Myanmar has repatriated nearly 10,000 migrants from Malaysia this year, state media said on Monday, a day after a flotilla returning almost 1,500 of its citizens docked in the country.
A group of 1,476 returnees arrived by ship outside Yangon on Sunday, the first of 5,000 that Kuala Lumpur says Myanmar agreed to take back.
Rights monitors have raised concerns that members of the Rohingya minority may be sent back to Myanmar, where they have faced violent persecution.
Myanmar revealed on Monday that a parallel and larger repatriation push has also been taking place by plane.
Between January and August this year, "8,041 citizens were repatriated by air", state newspaper The Global New Light of Myanmar said.
The total number of migrants Myanmar has said returned by plane and ship this year is 9,517.
Malaysia insists returnees under its scheme agreed to voluntary repatriation from detention centres, where Myanmar says they had "faced difficulties" after serving sentences for immigration offences.
But rights groups report dire conditions in the facilities, and the UN refugee agency says staff were not allowed to verify that decisions to return were "were genuinely free and informed."
More than 100,000 people are estimated to have been killed in Myanmar since a military coup in 2021 unleashed civil war, according to monitor organisation ACLED.

The Rohingya started fleeing the country en masse to Malaysia before that, escaping a military crackdown starting in 2017 deemed a genocide by rights groups – a charge the armed forces have always denied.
The Rohingya make up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in Malaysia, according to UN data.
After the ships carrying the 1,476 migrants docked Sunday in Thanlyin, just south of Yangon, AFP journalists saw dozens moved to a monastery holding centre for ID and health checks.

"Necessary arrangements are continuing to facilitate their swift reunion with relatives and family members, ensuring their safe return to their respective hometowns," The Global New Light of Myanmar said.
2d0f39e30861e642: TOKYO: Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields.
She said the government would pursue fiscal sustainability even as it ramps up spending to bolster growth potential, including by reviewing existing tax breaks and subsidies.
"Fiscal sustainability is obviously a prerequisite in pursuing our 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy," Takaichi said in a policy speech to parliament.
The remarks reflect mounting concern in Tokyo over rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields, which would boost the cost of funding the premier's ambitious spending plans.
The 30-year bond hit a record high of 4.235% on Monday on jitters over the risk of increased debt issuance and inflation worries fuelled by the Middle East war.

Japan's public debt, at roughly twice the size of its economy, is the largest in the developed world. Funding costs are climbing as the Bank of Japan raises interest rates and tapers bond purchases in an effort to wean the economy off decades of massive stimulus.
Takaichi said the government will seek to draw in private investment in growth areas through "massive, long-term fiscal expenditure deployed in a well-planned, predictable manner".

At the same time, it would keep a lid on annual bond issuance, calibrating borrowing to tax revenues, interest rates, debt-financing costs and economic and market developments, the premier said in the speech to an extraordinary parliament session that convened on Monday.
"If the economy and markets make unexpected moves, we will scrutinise their impact and respond nimbly as needed," she added without elaborating.
Fiscal policy is set to take centre stage in parliamentary debate in Japan as rising concerns over the fiscal health of advanced economies fuel a broader rise in global bond yields.

The administration's immediate priority is passing legislation backing Takaichi's plan for a two-year tax cut on food items from next April, which sparked a bond sell-off due to a lack of detail on how the revenue shortfall will be filled.
The government is also preparing next year's budget, with ministries seeking record levels of spending.
Separately, Takaichi said Tokyo will set aside multi-year funds for strategically important economic security initiatives.
"We will implement policies steadily, get things done one by one, and communicate them carefully to the public and markets," Takaichi said.

Keen to soothe market jitters, the administration has moved to dispel perceptions that its fiscal policy is reflationary or that it has leaned on the BOJ to refrain from hiking rates. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Saturday the government has begun refining its messaging to reassure investors that Takaichi is not pursuing reflationary policies.

But not all are on board. Former BOJ deputy governor Masazumi Wakatabe, a reflationist academic who is currently a private member of the government's key economic panel, said the recent rise in JGB yields was due to expectations of further BOJ rate hikes rather than concern over Japan's finances, minutes of the panel's recent meeting showed on Monday.

Wakatabe also said the government had ultimate responsibility in guiding economic policy and stressed the need for close coordination between the BOJ and the administration on monetary policy, according to the minutes of the meeting which debated the central bank's rate-hike decision last month.
af577abd0e4644a0: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry must expedite the recruitment and placement of nurses to address an 18 per cent vacancy rate in the public healthcare sector, the Malaysian Nurses Union (MNU) said.
MNU president Noor Aini Abu Hashim said all approved posts should be filled immediately to prevent staff shortages from further affecting healthcare services.
"We welcome efforts by the Public Service Commission (SPA) to expedite recruitment, including through open interviews.
"As of last September, SPA reported that more than 1,000 vacancies had been filled, but several hundred posts still need to be filled urgently," she said in a statement today.
Noor Aini said recruitment alone was insufficient to address the shortage, stressing that retention measures must also be strengthened.
She called for a review of salaries, allowances, shift incentives, speciality and specialisation allowances, as well as incentives for nurses posted to areas or facilities facing critical shortages.
"The ministry has stated that remuneration improvements are being considered to address competition for manpower," she said.
Noor Aini also urged the ministry to manage workloads and improve working conditions to reduce burnout among existing nurses.
She said work schedules, rest periods, leave and staffing requirements in every ward should reflect patient volume and complexity.
"Career pathways for nurses must also be accelerated. Nurses should have clear progression from diploma to degree, specialisation and leadership roles," she said.

While supporting efforts to increase trainee intake, Noor Aini said training capacity must be matched by clear placement planning to ensure graduates are effectively absorbed into the healthcare system.
She described the 18 per cent vacancy rate as a critical issue affecting the sustainability of the national healthcare system, rather than merely an administrative problem.
"The ministry previously reported that out of 73,281 Grade U5 nurse positions, 10,557 remained vacant as of August. This highlights a significant manpower gap.

"Nurses are among the largest healthcare groups working closest to patients. When staffing is inadequate, the workload shifts to existing nurses, affecting patient care, patient safety, productivity, staff morale and facility capacity," she said.
Noor Aini added that the MNU viewed the nursing shortage as an urgent issue requiring sustained, long-term action.
2791fd504ec8e8d2: KUALA LUMPUR: The financial position of households has remained generally resilient, supported by Malaysia's stable labour market conditions, according to Bank Negara Malaysia.

It said domestic policy measures, including expanded government cash assistance and continued fuel subsidies, have also helped contain the pass-through of higher global costs to domestic consumer prices.
"This has, in turn, limit the impact on household purchasing power and debt repayment capacity.
"The quality of household borrowings has remained largely stable," the central bank said in its Bank Negara Insights titled "Beyond Oil: From Geopolitical Conflict to Financial Stability Risk."

Looking at months-in-arrears (MIA) indicators, it said the MIA-2 and MIA-3 ratios, which indicate deeper repayment stress, increased marginally, while the MIA-1 ratio moderated significantly over the same period.
"This suggests that there has been no broad-based increase in new repayment difficulties among households," it said, adding that the demand for repayment assistance also remained broadly stable.
Collectively, these indicators provide limited evidence that the onset of the Middle East conflict has materially affected the household sector's debt repayment capacity.
Looking ahead, Bank Negara said micro-level indicators suggest that most household borrowers are well placed to weather potential shocks.
2d234dbef1650e18: KUALA LUMPUR: Cybersecurity should be treated as a national security priority rather than merely an information technology concern, as cyber breaches involving sensitive government data could have wider implications for the country, industry players said.

Aras Integrasi Sdn Bhd director of cybersecurity practice Faurani Jaafar said government agencies hold two broad categories of sensitive information, personal data belonging to citizens and information relating to the government itself (including details involving the procurement of assets).
"Even though we look at this from a cybersecurity perspective, our ability to prevent these incidents from happening actually contributes to national security.
"For example, if information relating to the procurement of military assets were compromised, other countries could potentially know what assets we are acquiring over the next three years.

"Our ability to protect national assets through cybersecurity initiatives such as this can therefore help improve national security," he told media at Cyber Digital Services, Defence & Security Asia (CyberDSA) 2026 here, today.

Aras Integrasi chief technology officer Farul Mohd Ghazali said the country should develop sufficient in-house capabilities to investigate cyber incidents rather than relying entirely on external technology providers.
He said local technology development should therefore focus not only on ownership but also on the ability to operate, maintain and continuously improve critical technology using local talent.
"Ultimately, we want to employ the best talent in Malaysia and ensure that these people can help us create better and better products.

"It is a perception issue that reduces the value that we can actually bring to the market. With all the talent that we have now and the capabilities in AI, what we see is equivalent to whatever you can get from overseas," said Farul.
Against this backdrop, Aras Integrasi has developed three homegrown cybersecurity platforms aimed at addressing different aspects of cyber risk and digital investigations.

The platforms comprise VoronCitadel, a governance, risk and compliance platform designed to help organisations manage cyber governance, digital risk, attack-surface visibility and third-party risk; GovSec, an AI-assisted threat intelligence platform that helps security teams identify and assess potential threats; and chainSENTRY, a blockchain intelligence and investigation platform for transaction tracing, wallet analysis and risk assessment.
The platforms were developed using local talent and technology, with GovSec developed in collaboration with CyberSecurity Malaysia.

Faurani said the platforms form part of Aras Integrasi's broader push for sovereign technology capabilities, with the company also seeking to use its own computing infrastructure to support research and development (R&D).
"We currently have 64 GPU units and do not rely on cloud infrastructure for our R&D. This gives our developers greater freedom to experiment and develop technology in-house," he said.
He added that the company was also looking to expand its collaboration with government agencies and eventually explore overseas markets as its technology matures.
